findings.title: Second downsize definition silently replaces the width/height API
findings.body: Ruby does not overload methods. `self.downsize(from, to, max_width, max_height, opts={})` at line 145 is immediately replaced by `self.downsize(from, to, dimensions, opts={})` at line 149, so the first method is dead. Any existing caller that passes numeric max width and max height (the previous public signature) now hits the new method: the width is treated as an ImageMagick geometry string and the height integer is treated as `opts`. `opts[:allow_animation]` then raises, or the convert command is built with a bogus geometry, so thumbnail downsizing elsewhere breaks.

findings.title: ImageMagick convert reads and writes the same tempfile path
findings.body: The new downsize loop calls `OptimizedImage.downsize(tempfile.path, tempfile.path, "80%", ...)`. `convert` (and gifsicle) are invoked with the same path as input and output. ImageMagick truncates the destination before it finishes reading the source when they are the same file, so the upload can be corrupted or emptied. The loop then keeps resizing that damaged file, and `Upload.create_for` still stores whatever is left.

findings.title: Oversized images are stored even when downsize fails or does not shrink enough
findings.body: The loop ignores the boolean returned by `OptimizedImage.downsize` and, after at most five attempts, always continues to `Upload.create_for` with the current tempfile. If convert fails, the file does not get smaller (percentage plus the `\>` shrink-only geometry often will not), or five 80% passes are not enough, the image is persisted above `SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb`. Combined with the client and `FileHelper.download` now allowing 10MB regardless of that setting, the configured image size limit is no longer enforced.

findings.title: Client size check hardcodes 10MB for every upload type
findings.body: `validateUploadedFile` used to compare against `Discourse.SiteSettings['max_' + type + '_size_kb']`, so images and attachments had independent admin limits. It now always uses `10 * 1024`. Attachments are no longer limited by `max_attachment_size_kb` (users can upload up to 10MB, or are blocked at 10MB if the admin allowed more). The 413 handler at line 246 has the same hardcode and always reports a 10MB image limit, so the error text is wrong for attachments and for any site whose real cap is not 10MB.

findings.title: API URL downloads ignore the configured size cap for non-images
findings.body: `FileHelper.download` used to stop at `SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb.kilobytes`. It now always fetches up to `10.megabytes` for every API URL upload, including attachments. Only filenames that `FileHelper.is_image?` enter the new downsize loop, so a non-image fetched from a URL can be stored at up to 10MB even when `max_attachment_size_kb` (or `max_image_size_kb`) is much smaller. That is a server-side bypass of the site setting, not just a client check.
